review_scope: Both complete Bambu A1 mini PETG archives. The carrier and loose OP1 sled change. The other twelve parts have the same mesh hashes, plate transforms and adhesion geometry as R64. All fourteen have material on the plate. The job uses a 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, separate timelapse tower and no generated supports.

op1_seat.socket_holes: On each exact slice, independent sampling of straight and arc extrusions through all ten layers of the sled slab, including nominal bead width and a 0.04 mm sampling allowance, gives clear centre-to-plastic radii of at least 1.749, 1.749 and 1.745 mm for the modelled 1.3 mm radius sockets. The retaining stops rise above the slab outside these holes.
op1_seat.switch_load: The sled prints flat, with both tabs integral with the slab in the layer plane. Plastic runs beneath the modelled press point through every 0.2–2.0 mm layer. Contact sections show 180.45 mm² beneath the PCB, including 88.94/91.51 mm² left/right and 22.45/22.44 mm² on the two halves of the switch footprint. The centred 2.9 × 1.2 mm press region has 2.72 mm² of contact. The R64 slice had only 0.21 mm² on the right and missed the press point by 1.201 mm.
op1_seat.receiver: At the carrier interface the printed left/right bearings measure 110.06/19.24 mm². A separate 0.1 mm raster of actual toolpaths, restricted to the permanent sled mesh, measures 5.98 and 9.38 mm² under the two outboard tabs on each slice. In CAD 20.09 mm² of the right bearing is still backed 1 mm below the landing, and the click line lies 6.31 mm inside the bearing polygon. These are load-path checks. Actual deflection and repeated-click durability need a fitted trial.
op1_seat.retention: The sled settles down 1.15 mm at the end of the slide. Checks at 24 directions found solid stops at 1 mm lateral translation with 0.25 mm lift. The upper keeper captures the PCB and the PCB captures the sled. Raising the PCB 0.35 mm enters the keeper by 15.35 mm³, and the raised keeper engages the unchanged guide. The precise front-loading keeper bead check clears both slices.
op1_seat.access: Load the wired board on the loose sled with the black switch out. Bring them up beside the rod from below, slide in white connector first, then drop into the receiver stops. The modelled complete moving assembly misses the full rod by 0.915 mm. Both slices clear all 69 tested routes, including the three sockets, connector body, plug and lead at the loose sled, the combined paths at the carrier, and the upper keeper. The sacrificial nose pad is at the opposite end from the connector and has two externally accessible one-layer ties.

native_warning.evidence: Both revised slices have zero wholly unsupported islands across all fourteen parts and zero generated support moves. Of 109 flagged carrier runs, 104 match R64 in layer, extent, length and anchoring, including the short rod mouth and two single-ended deck paths of 3.666 and 6.346 mm. The other five have both ends anchored: one 5.316 mm run on layer 74 and four runs of 1.312–3.647 mm on layer 155. The earlier isolated starts at layers 156 and 283 are gone. All six paddle runs and four post-bar runs match the previously printed R64 paths. The only sled run flagged by the layer scan is a 1.047 mm one-ended internal fill extension at layer 5. The slicer's internal floating-shell features at 1.0 and 1.2 mm are supported by the surrounding deposited slab; sparse-infill closure bridges span at most about 3.35 mm between prior-layer anchors in the sampled centreline check. No entirely free bridge line on the sled. The remaining ten parts have no flagged runs. The tower has a continuous root, and the slicer’s template lookup messages are covered by matching actual machine templates and first-object temperatures of 245/60 °C.

physical_checks: Monitor attachment of the complete plate including the nose pad and loose fittings. Cool the plate, support solid roots and cut the two nose ties and carrier fins. Inspect the socket bores and tabs after release.

Load the actual wired board while the switch is off. Slide, settle and fit the upper keeper. Confirm both tabs land, the board resists rocking under a press, and the switch clicks and releases with the keeper, real lead and paddle fitted. Compare the underside components with the assumed dimensions if it catches.

Check the real 8 mm rod, standard pin first, optional closer-fit pin with its flat correctly oriented, rear clip and wire. Test the guards, socket access, battery retention and removal, and repeated-click strength in the assembled holder.
plate_and_release: On both archives the sled has 373.27 mm² of connected first-layer footprint with 369.99 mm² of second-layer overlap. It prints flat with a two-layer nose pad and two 0.20 mm-high removable ties. Separate plate bases have at least 3.56 mm spacing. The carrier has 22.22 mm² of actual detachable-base fusion, zero on either free battery lip and zero at the hinge. The openings measure 3.364 mm through the assembled hinge and at least 8.300 mm for the rod. Deposited pin clearances at the best tested whole-pin pose are 0.2001 mm standard and 0.084 mm snug. Real pin fit, keeper force, print adhesion, support stiffness, pouch fit and long-term strength remain open physical checks.
